messages:
Maya (Design): Quick sync — notes from today's model-catalog review. Main issues: presets toggle is hidden in the filter rail, compare table's performance badge visually dominates name column, pinning a model/version feels transient, and some keyboard/focus/accessibility nits around badges. Short ideas below, please chime in.

Sana (PM): Agree re: presets toggle. Users expect presets to be top-level. Can we surface a compact 'Presets' segmented control above filters?

Tom (Product Eng): If we surface it we need to be explicit about scope: global presets vs. "apply to this compare". Could add a small checkbox: "Apply to compare" next to the segmented control.

Leo (Frontend): Badge styling is the main culprit — current drop shadow + full-bg makes them read as primary UI. Suggest: remove shadow, use subtle border + 10% desaturated bg. Also reduce font-size to 12px. Example CSS snippet: `.perf-badge{ background: var(--bg-10); border: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.06); font-size:12px; font-weight:600; padding:2px 6px; }`

Ash (Accessibility): Accessibility notes: badges only announce raw numbers. Need aria context. e.g. `aria-label="Performance: 98th percentile, median latency 220ms"`. Segmented control must use role="tablist"/tab or toggle buttons with `aria-pressed`. Also ensure keyboard order: Tab -> Compare table -> Badge action.

Maya (Design): Good calls. On pinning: current flow lets you pin a version but it clears when you navigate away. I think users expect pins to persist per-user (not just per-session). Is server storage required?

Sana (PM): User-scoped persistence preferred. Product question: should pin be workspace-level for teams? For MVP let's do user-scope, then evaluate workspace-level as a follow-up. Also need to capture analytics for pin/unpin events.

Tom (Product Eng): Implementation note: we can store user pin in localStorage and sync to backend on auth. Backend schema: user_pins { user_id, model_id, version, created_at }. We'll TTL or soft-delete on model retire.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: UI experiment `catalog/compare/preset-rail-v2` deployed to staging — https://staging.redwood.ai/catalog/compare (staging cluster).

Leo (Frontend): I'll pull staging tomorrow. Quick checklist for the change: 1) lighten badges, 2) add focus outline: `:focus{ outline: 3px solid rgba(37,99,235,0.12); }`, 3) ensure badges are reachable by keyboard (tabindex=0 if needed).

Maya (Design): Proposal (vote): 1) Move Presets to top of filter rail as segmented control + small "Apply to compare" checkbox, 2) Make badges visually lighter (no shadow, smaller font), 3) Make pinning persistent per-user (backend sync later), 4) Add aria-labels & focus styles for badges. React with :+1: to accept, :thinking_face: for questions, :x: to veto.

Tom (Product Eng): :+1:

Ash (Accessibility): :+1: on aria/focus changes, will review once deployed.

Sana (PM): :thinking_face: on analytics schema — will add event spec to the ticket.

Leo (Frontend): :+1: I'll start a PR to adjust badge CSS + focus states, will link shortly.

Maya (Design): Thanks — I'll update the prototype and add microcopy for the segmented control and the pin tooltip ("Pin version: keeps this version selected across sessions"). Will also add a short accessibility note in the ticket.

Tom (Product Eng): One minor UX nit: when pin is active and you open compare with multiple rows selected, pin should not auto-select the pinned row if it's not part of the current compare — we should show a toast: "Pinned version not in this selection".

Maya (Design): Agree. Add toast copy: "Pinned version not included in this compare — open model to see pinned version."

Sana (PM): I'll create the Jira with acceptance criteria: presets control, badge style, pin persistence, analytics, accessibility checks. ETA: next week.

Maya (Design): Great — thanks everyone. Follow-ups in the ticket; I'll paste prototype and staging link once updated. :sparkles:
